subject: English
passage: Members of the Tavaran community in the highlands of northern Sulawesi share festival grounds with members of the neighboring Kelanu community, whose elders utter a distinctive chant to announce the start of a harvest blessing. Anthropologists Padma Hayashi and Suresh Hayashi recorded Kelanu blessing chants and played them during ordinary gatherings attended by Tavaran participants. Observing that Tavaran attendees frequently paused their conversations and gathered toward the center of the grounds upon hearing the chants, they concluded that Tavaran attendees associate Kelanu blessing chants with an imminent ceremonial event.
prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Hayashi and Hayashi's conclusion?

choices.A: Hayashi and Hayashi played blessing chants recorded from different Kelanu elders and observed no significant variation in the responses of Tavaran attendees.
choices.B: When Hayashi and Hayashi played control recordings of unrelated instrumental music during ordinary gatherings, Tavaran attendees showed no change in behavior.
choices.C: In some instances Tavaran attendees paused their conversations and gathered toward the center of the grounds when Hayashi and Hayashi arrived but before any recordings were played.
choices.D: Members of communities other than Tavaran also tended to pause their conversations and gather toward the center of the grounds when Hayashi and Hayashi played Kelanu blessing chants.

explanation:
Choice B is the best answer because it presents a finding that, if true, would most directly support the researchers' conclusion that Tavaran attendees associate Kelanu blessing chants with an imminent ceremonial event. The text explains that Hayashi and Hayashi observed Tavaran attendees pausing their conversations and gathering toward the center upon hearing recorded Kelanu chants, leading them to conclude that the attendees associate those chants with an impending ceremony. If the attendees displayed no change in behavior when unrelated instrumental music was played as a control, that finding would support the conclusion by demonstrating that the attendees' response was specific to the Kelanu chants rather than a general reaction to any audio played during a gathering.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect because finding that Tavaran attendees showed no significant variation in responses to chants recorded from different Kelanu elders would address the consistency of the attendees' reactions across sources but wouldn't directly support the conclusion that they associate the chants with a ceremonial event. This finding would simply show that the response is uniform, but it wouldn't rule out alternative explanations for why the attendees react.
